The fix is commit `21ea98bd` (PR #6537, ticket TRUNK-6796, "Fix NPE when death date is null when merging patients"). It changed the null-check in `PersonMergeLogData.computeHashValue()` from `getPriorDateOfBirth() != null` to `getPriorDateOfDeath() != null`. The line before it guarded the date of birth, so a null prior date of death was dereferenced by `.toString()` whenever the date of birth was set. The commit also added `PersonMergeLogDataTest`, which sets only a prior date of birth and asserts that `computeHashValue()` does not throw.

Evidence, best first:

1. `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogData.java:445`: the corrected null-check, which is the line that carries the fix.
2. `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogData.java:392-448`: the full `computeHashValue()` method, including the neighbouring date-of-birth line (444).
3. `openmrs-core/api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogDataTest.java:18-27`: the regression test added with the fix.
4. `openmrs-core/api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/PersonServiceTest.java:1510-1514`: an existing test that compares hash values across a merge-log save and retrieve. It is related, not the fix itself.
